tools.name: mloop_train
tools.description: Train an ML model using AutoML. Runs mloop train command with specified parameters. Answers the run's result (experiment id, trainer, metrics, promotion) and warnings as JSON; reports progress per trial when the call carries a progress token; cancelling the call stops the run. Without time, the run sizes its own budget from the data.

dataFile.description: Training data file (default: data.train in mloop.yaml, else datasets/train.csv; with additionalDataFiles and no dataFile, datasets/train.csv)

task.description: ML task type (default: the project's, from mloop.yaml)

maxTrials.description: Stop the trainer search after this many trials, within time — the same search on a fast machine and a slow one. Tasks that run no search (clustering, anomaly detection, recommendation, forecasting, deep learning) refuse it

epochs.description: Epochs a deep-learning task trains for (default 10): text classification, sentence similarity, NER, question answering, object detection. `time` does not shorten such a fit, so this is its one dial on cost — try 2 first to see what an epoch costs. Other tasks refuse it

balance.description: Class balancing strategy for classification (image classification included — it oversamples its training split): "auto" (balance to 10:1), "none", or target ratio (e.g., "5" for 5:1)

dropMissingLabels.description: Drop rows with missing label values before training

weight.description: Column that weights the rows (e.g. 1/π for sampled labels); never a feature

additionalDataFiles.description: Files merged after dataFile (e.g. a retraining set from mloop_sample create); a file without the weight column counts its rows 1

portable.description: Train only with steps ONNX can express, so mloop_export_onnx can export the model

ensemble.description: Answer with a weighted blend of the search's best trials when it scores better out of fold (binary classification and regression; another task refuses it). A blend is one model file several times larger and a single-row request to a served model takes several times as long; mloop_export_onnx refuses it and it cannot be combined with `portable`

groupColumn.description: Ranking: the column that groups rows into query contexts

encoder.description: image-anomaly: the installed image encoder the pictures are embedded with (default: the only one installed — see mloop_encoder)

bankSize.description: image-anomaly: the most patches the bank holds; a limit keeps a coreset of the patches (default: every patch)

maxRows.description: Most training rows; more are sampled

samplingStrategy.description: How rows are sampled when maxRows applies (default: by task)

records.description: For a JSON data file: the dotted path to the array whose items are the rows

analyzeData.description: Check the data quality and train nothing: the answer carries `analysis` (each finding with a suggested fix; an empty list when there are none) instead of a result

generateScript.description: Write a preprocessing script from the data check to this path. With analyzeData the run stops there (the answer carries `script`); without it, it goes on to train

autoMerge.description: Detect and merge the CSV files of the same schema in datasets/ into the training data

autoTime.description: true: size the time budget from the data even when mloop.yaml sets one; false: no estimation, the 300 s default budget; leave out: the run decides (a given `time` always wins)

tools.name: mloop_predict
tools.description: Run predictions using a trained model. Uses production model by default; `experimentId` predicts with that experiment instead (a shadow prediction — production does not move). The JSON names the model that answered in `experimentId`.

dataFile.description: Prediction data file (default: data.predict in mloop.yaml, else datasets/predict.csv)

experimentId.description: Predict with this experiment (e.g. a staging candidate) instead of production — production does not move

model.description: Path to a model file to predict with instead of the production model

log.description: Log the predictions; without an output file each returned row carries the predictionId that feedback takes

includeFeatures.description: Whether the output file repeats the input feature columns (the CLI default is yes; false leaves them out)

records.description: For a JSON data file: the dotted path to the array whose items are the rows

unknownStrategy.description: Strategy for handling unknown categorical values in prediction data

scoreThreshold.description: Object detection only: report boxes with at least this confidence (default 0.5). A detector trained by MLoop since the ranked metrics keeps every box down to 0.05, so 0.3 (then lower) shows what a not-yet-confident detector finds; an older model keeps only boxes of 0.5 and over

tools.name: mloop_list
tools.description: List all experiments and their metrics for a model.

trials.description: An experiment ID: show its trial leaderboard (every candidate the search tried, e.g. a clustering run's K = 2..10) instead of the experiment overview

tools.name: mloop_promote
tools.description: Promote an experiment to production. Select by explicit ID, or auto-select with latest (newest completed) / best (best metric, direction-aware). The promoted model will be used for predictions. With history, lists every change of production instead — experiment, what it replaced, action (promote / auto-promote / rollback), the quality gate outcome (passed / forced / not-applied) and the metric value (mloop >= 0.39).

experimentId.description: Experiment ID to promote (e.g., exp-003); omit when using latest/best

latest.description: Promote the most recent completed experiment

best.description: Promote the completed experiment with the best metric (direction-aware)

force.description: Skip confirmation, and promote a model the quality gate refuses

history.description: List every change of production instead of promoting (mloop >= 0.39)

decideOnly.description: Report which experiment latest/best would promote, and move nothing — the production model stays as it is

tools.name: mloop_rollback
tools.description: Return production to the experiment it held before the current one (from the promotion history), backing up the current production first. With "to", return to a named experiment that has been production before; an experiment that never served is refused — use mloop_promote for that.

to.description: Experiment to return to; it must have been in production before (default: the one the current production replaced)

tools.name: mloop_threshold
tools.description: A binary classifier's decision threshold, as JSON. With precision and dataFile, chooses the probability threshold at which the precision of the positive class — or of precisionOf, the negative one included (mloop >= 0.40) — reaches the target on those labeled rows, keeping the most of that class's recall, and writes it beside the model — predict, serve, evaluate and the gate then answer at it, and promote carries it. With guarantee (a risk such as 0.05, mloop >= 0.48) the threshold is the lowest one whose precision is certified, not merely observed on the file — the usual choice is the luckiest reading of its rows, and on synthetic files its true precision fell below the target about half the time; a certified one needs enough rows (29 right answers for 0.90 at 0.05) and is refused, writing nothing, when the file cannot carry it. Without precision, shows the current one; with clear, removes it. Refused for a model that is not binary or gives no probability, or when no threshold reaches the precision (mloop >= 0.39).

experimentId.description: Experiment to set the threshold of (default: the production model)

precision.description: Target positive precision (above 0, at most 1): the lowest threshold reaching it on dataFile is chosen

precisionOf.description: The class whose precision is targeted, by its label value (default: the positive class) — the negative class too, when a wrong "no" is the costly answer

guarantee.description: Risk δ, above 0 and below 1 (e.g. 0.05), with precision: choose the lowest threshold whose precision is certified to reach the target — wrong in at most δ of the files it could be run on — or refuse when the file cannot carry it (mloop >= 0.48)

dataFile.description: Labeled evaluation file the threshold is chosen on (required with precision)

clear.description: Remove the threshold: the model answers at 0.5 again

records.description: For a JSON dataFile: the dotted path to the array whose items are the rows

tools.name: mloop_calibrate
tools.description: A classifier's probability calibration, as JSON. With dataFile, fits a map from the model's own probability to how often it is right on those labeled rows (binary: platt or isotonic; multiclass: temperature, answers unchanged; weighted rows allowed) and writes it beside the model without retraining — predict, serve, evaluate (its ECE) and a threshold chosen afterwards then read calibrated probabilities, and promote carries it. Reports ECE before and after on the fit rows (in-sample). Refused while the model has a decision threshold (clear it, calibrate, choose it again). Without dataFile, shows the current one; with clear, removes it (mloop >= 0.40).

experimentId.description: Experiment to calibrate (default: the production model)

dataFile.description: Labeled rows the calibration is fit on — rows the model was not trained on

method.description: Binary: platt (default; steady on a few hundred rows) or isotonic (no shape assumed, needs more rows). Multiclass: temperature (default; answers unchanged)

weight.description: Column that weights the rows (1/π for a recheck sample)

clear.description: Remove the calibration: the model answers with its own probabilities again

records.description: For a JSON dataFile: the dotted path to the array whose items are the rows

tools.name: mloop_export_onnx
tools.description: Write a trained model (binary, multiclass or regression) as an ONNX graph plus a manifest (model.onnx.json) naming each graph input and the data columns behind it, the outputs, the classes, the metrics and SHA-256 hashes — for runtimes without ML.NET. A model that featurizes a free-text column with the ML.NET text featurizer is refused with the columns named — train it with `portable: true` (mloop_train) to export it; a category column exports as is.

experimentId.description: Experiment to export (default: the production model)

dataFile.description: A data file with the model's input columns (default: the experiment's training file)

outputDir.description: Directory for model.onnx and model.onnx.json (default: the experiment's directory)

verify.description: Run the graph in ONNX Runtime and compare it with the model; a graph that disagrees is not kept

tools.name: mloop_info
tools.description: Analyze and profile a dataset. Shows column types, statistics, missing values, and more. Can read label column from mloop.yaml configuration.

dataFile.description: Path to data file to analyze

projectPath.description: MLoop project path (optional, for relative paths)

modelName.description: Model name to read label configuration from mloop.yaml (default: "default")

analyze.description: Enable deep analysis including correlation, feature importance, distribution, and anomaly detection

sampleSize.description: Maximum number of rows to sample for deep analysis (default: 50000)

records.description: For a JSON data file: the dotted path to the array whose items are the rows

tools.name: mloop_status
tools.description: Show MLoop project status including models, experiments, and production deployments.

verbose.description: Detailed status: more than the overview of each model

tools.name: mloop_compare
tools.description: Compare metrics across multiple experiments to identify the best performing model.

experiments.description: Experiment IDs to compare (at least 2; leave out to compare the model's completed experiments)

best.description: Compare only the top N experiments by metric (without experiments)

metric.description: Rank by this metric instead of the one the model was trained to optimize

metricsFile.description: Rank candidates from a JSON file of metrics, with no MLoop project needed (an external system of record's candidates): [{"id": ..., "metrics": {...}}, ...]

tools.name: mloop_evaluate
tools.description: Evaluate a model's performance on test data, as JSON: test metrics beside the training metrics, per slice with sliceBy, weighted with weight. For a classifier, confusion: classes and counts[actual][predicted] (weighted sums under weight; per slice too) — read any class-set rate from it, e.g. the share of a must-catch class answered as a harmless one (mloop >= 0.39). With against (an experiment id or "production"), the other model is scored on the same rows and weights and the two are compared row by row: comparison.metrics, and comparison.paired — the per-row loss (error_rate for a classifier, squared_error for a regressor) of each, their difference (candidate − baseline), a 95% paired bootstrap interval, and verdict CandidateBetter / BaselineBetter / Indistinguishable. Use it to decide whether a staging candidate should replace production.

dataFile.description: Test data file for evaluation (default: data.test in mloop.yaml, else datasets/test.csv)

sliceBy.description: Also report the metrics for each value of this column of the test data

weight.description: Column that weights the test rows (defaults to the experiment's training weight when the file has it)

normalClass.description: image-anomaly: the subfolder of the test folder that holds the normal pictures (default: normal, good or ok); every other subfolder is anomalous (mloop >= 0.47)

records.description: For a JSON test file: the dotted path to the array whose items are the rows

against.description: Also evaluate this experiment id (or "production") on the same rows and weights, and compare the two row by row (mloop >= 0.39)

tools.name: mloop_serve
tools.description: Start the MLoop REST API server for serving predictions via HTTP. Returns once the server answers /health, with its URL, process id, log file and the command that stops it; the server keeps running after the call.

tools.name: mloop_init
tools.description: Initialize a new MLoop project. Creates mloop.yaml, datasets/, models/ directories.

projectPath.description: Path to create/initialize the MLoop project

task.description: ML task type for this project

label.description: Label column name (can be set later in mloop.yaml; default: "Label")

tools.name: mloop_validate
tools.description: Validate the mloop.yaml configuration file. Checks for syntax errors, missing fields, and invalid values.

tools.name: mloop_prep
tools.description: Run a model's preprocessing pipeline — the prep steps declared under the model in mloop.yaml (see mloop_prep_plan) — over a CSV file, writing the prepared file.

modelName.description: Model whose prep steps (mloop.yaml) to run (default: 'default')

input.description: Input CSV file (default: data.train in mloop.yaml, else datasets/train.csv)

dryRun.description: Show the pipeline steps without executing them

tools.name: mloop_logs
tools.description: View prediction logs for a model. Shows recent predictions with timestamps and results.

limit.description: Maximum number of log entries to show

from.description: Only entries from this day on (yyyy-MM-dd)

to.description: Only entries up to this day (yyyy-MM-dd)

tools.name: mloop_feedback
tools.description: Manage feedback for model predictions. Add the actual value for a logged prediction (with its source and an optional weight), list existing feedback, or view feedback metrics (accuracy is weighted when feedback carries weights).

predictionId.description: Prediction ID to add feedback for (required for "add")

source.description: Where the value came from, e.g. "human", "reviewer-llm" (for "add")

weight.description: How much this row counts in training and evaluation built from feedback — for a row reviewed with probability p, 1/p (for "add"; default 1)

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to show (for "list"; default 20)

from.description: Only entries from this day on (yyyy-MM-dd; for "list" and "metrics")

to.description: Only entries up to this day (yyyy-MM-dd; for "list" and "metrics")

tools.name: mloop_sample
tools.description: Create a sampled dataset — from a model's logged predictions and feedback (a retraining dataset: feedback under the model's label, with a weight column when feedback carries weights) or from a data file (CSV, TSV, JSON, Excel, Parquet; written as CSV) — or view sampling statistics.

modelName.description: Model whose logged predictions and feedback to sample ("create": a retraining dataset — the feedback under the model's label, weighted when feedback carries weights; "stats": default "default")

dataFile.description: Data file to sample from instead of prediction logs — CSV, TSV, JSON, Excel or Parquet; the sample is written as CSV ("create" only)

records.description: For a JSON data file: the dotted path to the array whose items are the rows ("create" only)

strategy.description: Sampling strategy — logs: random, recent, feedback-priority, stratified, low-confidence; CSV: random, head, stratified

label.description: Label column for stratified CSV sampling

tools.name: mloop_trigger
tools.description: Check whether retraining is due, as JSON: each default condition — feedback accuracy (the production experiment's own answers, met once the drop is established: at least 30 rows of feedback and the 95% interval's upper end below the threshold), feedback volume, time since training and input drift (PSI of the production model's logged inputs against its training data, met at 0.25) — with its threshold, current value, whether it is met and why; the drift condition carries every column's PSI under drift. A condition that could not be measured says so in details.

accuracy.description: Accuracy threshold (0.0-1.0): the accuracy condition is met when feedback accuracy drops below it (default: the project's)

feedback.description: Feedback volume threshold: the volume condition is met once this many feedback rows have come in (default: the project's)

tools.name: mloop_drift
tools.description: How far the production model's recent inputs (its own logged predictions) have moved from the data it was trained on, as JSON: status (Measured, NoProduction, NoProfile, TooFewRows), and per column the population stability index (PSI — under 0.1 stable, 0.1–0.25 moderate, 0.25+ significant), its level and the bin that moved most with its training and current share; plus, under drift.prediction, the same measure for the model's own answers against its answers at training (predicted class, or predicted value by decile; null when the model has no answer profile — mloop >= 0.39). A free-text column appears as two columns, "<column> (length)" and "<column> (unseen words)" — the share of words training never saw, the one that moves when the text changes subject (mloop >= 0.40). With sliceBy, the same per value of an input column. Answers that move while inputs hold mean the mix of requests shifted inside known ranges. Use it to decide where to look harder or whether to retrain (mloop >= 0.38).

rows.description: How many of the most recent logged predictions to compare (default 5000, at least 100)

sliceBy.description: Also report drift per value of this input column (values with 100+ predictions)

tools.name: mloop_analyze
tools.description: Run a single, read-only exploratory-data-analysis (EDA) aspect on a dataset and return a structured JSON envelope for feature-engineering decisions. Aspects: profile, correlation, importance (needs a label), outliers, distribution, series (a column as an ordered series). Never mutates the data file or mloop.yaml.

aspect.description: EDA aspect to compute: "profile" (column types, null %, cardinality, constant columns), "correlation" (high-correlation pairs + multicollinearity), "importance" (feature-importance ranking, requires a label), "outliers" (count/rate/isolation-forest threshold), "distribution" (skewness/kurtosis/normality tests), "series" (one column read as an ordered series: autocorrelation/partial autocorrelation with their bands, ADF and KPSS stationarity tests read together, dominant period; needs mloop 0.48 or later)

dataFile.description: Path to the CSV dataset to analyze. Optional: when omitted, defaults to the project's configured train data (data.train in mloop.yaml, else datasets/train.csv). Pass projectPath so the default can be resolved.

projectPath.description: MLoop project path (for resolving relative paths and the default data file)

label.description: Label/target column name (overrides mloop.yaml; required for the "importance" aspect)

column.description: Series column to analyze (only the "series" aspect; optional when the CSV has a single column)

maxLag.description: Largest lag of the autocorrelation functions (only "series"; default min(10*log10 n, n - 1))

aroundTrend.description: Test stationarity around a linear trend instead of a constant level (only "series")

modelName.description: Model name to read label configuration from mloop.yaml (default: "default")

records.description: For a JSON data file: the dotted path to the array whose items are the rows

tools.name: mloop_detect
tools.description: One-shot time-series anomaly detection over an entire CSV series (spectral residual, no training, no MLoop project required). Every point returns an anomaly verdict (isAnomaly), its score, an expectedValue and control limits (controlLower/controlUpper — the chartable band normal points lie inside); nearEdge marks points too close to the end of the series to judge as surely. Use this instead of train+predict when analyzing a whole series once.

dataPath.description: Path to the CSV file containing the time series

column.description: Value column to monitor (auto-selected when the CSV has a single column)

threshold.description: Score above which a point is an anomaly (> 0; the score is a point's saliency relative to the points before it; default 3)

sensitivity.description: Coverage of the control limits in percent (0-100, exclusive; 99.73 = 3 sigma; default 99.73)

output.description: Also write the full per-point result to this CSV file

records.description: For a JSON data file: the dotted path to the array whose items are the rows

tools.name: mloop_prep_plan
tools.description: Declare a preprocessing step in mloop.yaml (policy only — never changes data). Add/replace with set='type[:method]' (+ optional columns), remove with remove='type', or omit both to list the current plan. Returns a JSON envelope where each step reports its leakage category (preFeaturizer/csvStage/unsupportedLeakageWarn) and fold-safety. Statistical fit happens fold-internally at train time.

projectPath.description: Path to the MLoop project directory

columns.description: Comma-separated target columns for the --set/--remove step (e.g. "a,b")

remove.description: Remove prep step(s) of this type

tools.name: mloop_features_select
tools.description: Declare which columns are features in mloop.yaml (policy only — never changes data). Exclude columns with drop='a,b', keep only certain columns with keep='a,b' (all others excluded, label always kept), or clear all exclusions with reset=true. Returns a JSON envelope listing the excluded (ignored) columns.

projectPath.description: Path to the MLoop project directory

drop.description: Comma-separated columns to exclude from features (e.g. "id,ts")

keep.description: Comma-separated columns to keep; all other columns are excluded (label always kept)

tools.name: mloop_token
tools.description: Issue a JWT bearer token for a server started with mloop_serve: every endpoint but /health requires one, sent as the returned Authorization header. Signed with the development key unless key is given; role admin for the write endpoints.

role.description: admin for the write endpoints (POST /promote, /rollback, /train, /evaluate, /samples, cache); omit for predict and reads

subject.description: Who the token identifies (the sub claim); the request limit counts per subject (default: mloop-cli)

key.description: The server's signing key (Jwt:Key), when it is not the development key — at least 32 characters

tools.name: mloop_embed
tools.description: Turn images or texts into L2-normalised vectors with a pretrained encoder (mloop_encoder installs one), with the encoder's identity — id, sha256, preprocessor — so vectors from different encoders or versions are never compared. Texts need mloop 0.46.0 or later.

projectPath.description: Working directory the paths are relative to (an MLoop project is not required)

images.description: Image files (PNG, JPEG, …) to embed, at most 64

texts.description: Texts to embed with a text encoder, at most 256 — instead of images

encoder.description: The encoder to use (mloop_encoder list); may be left out when only one of the kind is installed

patches.description: Also one vector per patch of each image, on the encoder's grid (images only, at most 8)

textFile.description: A UTF-8 file of texts to embed, one per line (at most 256 together with texts) — instead of images

tools.name: mloop_encoder
tools.description: Manage the pretrained encoders mloop_embed and encoder-read text columns run: list the installed ones, install a catalog encoder (its weights are downloaded and checked against a pinned SHA-256 — dinov2-small ~88 MB, multilingual-minilm ~470 MB), add one of your own from its definition file and ONNX graph (and tokenizer, for a text encoder), or remove one.

projectPath.description: Working directory (encoders are kept per user, not per project)

action.description: list the installed encoders, install one from the catalog, add one of your own from its files, or remove one

encoder.description: The encoder id — for install, a catalog id (dinov2-small for images, multilingual-minilm for text); for remove, an installed one

tokenizer.description: add, a text encoder: its tokenizer model (SentencePiece .model)

tools.name: mloop_explain
tools.description: Which input columns a trained model relies on, as JSON: permutation importance on a labeled file, in the metric mloop_evaluate reports — each column is shuffled `repeats` times and the importance is the mean drop (± the spread), at most `rows` rows, seeded so the same seed gives the same numbers. A column the model did not read is listed as not shuffled. It is reliance, not cause: correlated columns share it. Defaults to the production model and datasets/test.csv (needs an mloop newer than 0.48).

experimentId.description: Experiment to explain (default: the production model)

dataFile.description: Labeled file the model is scored on, with the label column (default: data.test in mloop.yaml, else datasets/test.csv)

weight.description: Column that weights the rows (defaults as mloop_evaluate does)

repeats.description: Shuffles per column; the importance is their mean (default 3)

rows.description: Most rows scored; a larger file is sampled — every column costs repeats scorings (default 2000)

seed.description: Seed of the sample and the shuffles: the same seed gives the same numbers (default 1)

records.description: For a JSON data file: the dotted path to the array whose items are the rows

tools.name: mloop_runtime
tools.description: Manage the deep-learning runtimes mloop downloads on demand: list them with their install state, install one (tf for image classification, torch for text tasks, onnxruntime for the ONNX export check and image encoders — a large download), or remove it. A task whose runtime is missing refuses to train and names the runtime to install.

projectPath.description: Working directory (runtimes are kept per user, not per project)

action.description: list the runtimes and whether each is installed, install one, or remove an installed one

runtime.description: The runtime to install or remove: tf (image classification), torch (text tasks), onnxruntime (ONNX export check, image encoders)

tools.name: mloop_docker
tools.description: Generate the Docker configuration that serves a project's model with `mloop serve` (a Dockerfile and a docker-compose.yml, whose compose service mounts the project's models read-only and needs a JWT_SIGNING_KEY of 32+ characters to start) into the project directory. Files already there are overwritten. Answers the console text: this command has no JSON output.

projectPath.description: Path to MLoop project directory (the files are written here)

port.description: Port the API is exposed on (default 5000)

tools.name: mloop_quick_start
tools.description: One-step project setup: initialize -> train -> auto-promote. Provide data file, label, and task type to go from zero to production model.

dataFile.description: Training data: a CSV (or other table) file, or for the image tasks a folder of pictures

label.description: Label column name (omit for tasks that learn without one: clustering, anomaly-detection, image-anomaly, ...)

time.description: Training time in seconds (omit for auto-time)

tools.name: mloop_auto_train
tools.description: Automated training pipeline: profile data -> train (with auto-time) -> list experiments. Handles the full training workflow in a single call.

dataFile.description: Training data file (default: data.train in mloop.yaml, else datasets/train.csv)

label.description: Label column (uses mloop.yaml default if omitted)

tools.name: mloop_project_overview
tools.description: Get a comprehensive overview of the MLoop project: status, all experiments, and production model metrics in a single call.
